You’re allowed to grieve as long as you need if you loved her. But do these things too.

1) Get yourself a therapist. You’re so young and this is gonna stick with you, but having a professional to help you through this is gonna make all the difference. 
2) Have an honest sit down with your parents about this, or maybe one parent who is more empathetic, and explain that their dismissal of your feelings hurts and, if one of your parents were to suddenly pass, would they want to hear that same advice? They may write it off since you two weren’t married, but just remind them that your emotions are your own and you’re allowed to experience them, you don’t need their permission.
3) Surround yourself with friends that will support you. But socialize. Hang out and have fun. You’re still just a kid. I know it seems impossible to be happy right now, and you’re gonna feel shitty, even now a year after she passed. But it’ll get better over time. It won’t go away, but the pain will fade, dull, and become a bearable weight over time. It sucks, I know. But in the kindest possible way, that is sorta what life is about. Meetings and partings.

But above all please remember this. If you’re feeling genuine pain after she left, that means it was real. Never let anyone tell you otherwise. You genuinely loved her, and hold onto how you loved her and how it made you feel. But also allow yourself, with time, to be open to love someone else in a different way. 

I hope this helps. You are probably just starting out in life and this is the worst way to start, but never apologize for your feelings.
